Software wise, webrtc https://webrtc.org/, VLC http://www.videolan.org/vlc/ can do it, also OBS https://obsproject.com/

Then you need a basic webserver/scripting setup and some html5, I'd recommend something like nginx/php-fpm/memcache to get set up quickly with a user interface and whatnot. I've found this setup to perform pretty comparable in load to tomcat in practice, although tomcat often falls over sooner and becomes unresponsive. In the end though the work either would do would be kind of light weight, handling logins and setting up streams, etc...

For db i'd suggest MariaDB, but it doesn't need to be a heavy lifter so you can use whatever.

7 Habits for Effective Text Editing 2.0 (2007) - Bram Moolenaar (1:20:29, half is QA)

The text editor Vim, 25 years old, is a clone of 39-year-old vi. Of course you'll need plugins for a program that was made to run on computers that barely had memory or processing power. Some of the plugins (or alternatives) most vim users should have :

Vundle: plug-in manager

Ultisnips: The ultimate snippet solution for Vim. Vim-snippets has a great collection of default snippets for most languages.

YouCompleteMe: A code-completion engine for Vim. Instead of doing CTRL-X, CTRL-O to start auto complete, it auto-completes/intellisenses everything as you type.

Ctrl-p: Fuzzy file, buffer, mru, tag, etc finder. If you have it, update the plugin location from kein (no longer active) to ctrlpvim (actively developed fork.)

Syntastic: Syntax checking hacks for vim.

Easymotion: Vim motions on speed. I love the "hjkl motions" section.

There's plenty of other plugins that are specific to a language or situation. For the languages that don't work well with YouCompleteMe (Java, possibly others) there's Eclim (the power of Eclipse in your favorite editor: vim and, with third party clients, emacs, sublime text 2, textmate.)
